title: Privileged-access delegation request flow and risk-tagging
creator: Aisha Carter
description: Goal: Define and implement a standardized intake and approval workflow for privileged/privilege-delegation requests (e.g., org admins, billing admins, delegated auditors) that combines automated risk-tagging with human approvals. Scope includes RBAC role templates, SSO/SAML onboarding exceptions, SCIM provisioning edge-cases, and organization policy overrides. Deliverables: 1) a decision tree for automatic vs manual handling, 2) a risk-tagging rubric surfaced in intake UI, 3) approval escalation paths and SLAs, 4) audit metadata schema and retention requirements, 5) a lightweight operator runbook for edge cases.
acceptance_criteria: A decision tree doc that maps request attributes to auto-approve, needs-approval, or deny, linked in Confluence
Risk-tagging rubric implemented as discrete labels on intake items (risk: low|medium|high) and visible in console
UI mockups for intake form including justification, requested duration, and temporary delegation checkbox reviewed by Design
Approval policy engine config prototype that can reference role templates and require 1- or 2-step approvals based on risk
Audit log schema defined and validated with Security (fields: actor, request_id, justification, duration, rationale, approver_chain)
E2E intake->approval->provisioning smoke test that uses SCIM patch for delegation provisioning and verifies audit entry

comments: 2025-02-13 - Mateo: Spiked the approval-engine prototype and confirmed we can express 2-step approvals via existing policy DSL. Need a small API extension to persist approver_chain.

2025-02-28 - Riley (Solutions): Collected 3 customer request examples: 1) finance team billing admin (medium risk), 2) external auditor temporary auditor role (high risk, 7 days), 3) platform integrator SCIM bulk mapping (low risk if scoped). Using these to validate rubric thresholds.
2025-03-01 - Mateo: Estimate finalized at 5 points. Blocker: infra work to add immutable audit store for request writes (ENG-1842). Scheduled eng sync for 2025-03-03.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive auto-approve reduces toil but increases risk — mitigation via short duration limits and automatic re-eval after provision window expires.
Consider implementing a 'just-in-time' delegation token that auto-expires and requires re-authorization via SSO to renew.
Potential future: expose a delegated-access dashboard to tenant admins showing active delegations and upcoming expirations (post-MVP).
